description: Cross-product rules (UDAAP lexicon, badge qualifiers, substantiation, urgency, endorsements, soft-pull claims). RulebookEntry.product is single-valued, so each conceptual rule is expanded into three concrete entries sharing a family prefix: XP-<FAMILY>-<NNN>-<product>.

parameters.check_description: Approval-certainty phrases like 'guaranteed approval' or 'no credit check' are banned outright wherever any underwriting exists.

rules.explanation: UDAAP/FTC Act Section 5 lexicon: approval-certainty phrases are deceptive wherever any underwriting or screening exists. These are per-se prohibited across products.

parameters.judge_focus: Superlative/comparative claims ('lowest rates', 'best loan', 'beats any offer'): is there plausible current-market substantiation, or is this a measurable claim presented without basis? Distinguish puffery ('great rates') from measurable superlatives ('lowest APR available').
violation_examples: The lowest personal loan rates in America — guaranteed to beat any competitor.
Nobody approves more borrowers than ClearPath. (measurable market-share claim, no basis)
parameters.compliant_contrast: Great rates for qualified borrowers — APR from 8.99% to 35.99% based on creditworthiness.
parameters.citation_quote: Exaggerated claims or “puffery,” however, are not deceptive if the claims would not be taken seriously by a reasonable consumer.

rules.explanation: FTC substantiation doctrine as adopted in CFPB UDAAP examination standards: objective comparative claims require a reasonable basis at the time they are made. Measurable superlatives without substantiation are deceptive; pure puffery is not.

parameters.judge_focus: Superlative/comparative claims ('lowest rates', 'best mortgage'): is there plausible current-market substantiation? Reg N 1014.3 additionally bans misrepresenting comparisons between mortgage products, including partial-period comparisons.
violation_examples: Save $800/month versus your current mortgage (comparison built on the ARM's teaser period only)
Guaranteed lowest refinance rates in your state.
parameters.compliant_contrast: Compare our current 30-year fixed rates — updated daily — against your existing loan terms.
parameters.citation_quote: It is a violation of this part for any person to make any material misrepresentation, expressly or by implication, in any commercial communication, regarding any term of any mortgage credit product

rules.explanation: FTC substantiation doctrine plus Reg N comparison prohibitions: objective comparative mortgage claims require a reasonable basis; comparisons using less than the full loan term are banned.

parameters.check_description: Urgency devices ('act now', 'expires today') are flagged unless the referenced offer really expires when the ad implies.
parameters.note: effective_end_supports_urgency is derived by the checker from the offer cell's effective_end.

rules.explanation: Fake-urgency devices are deceptive dark patterns unless the offer genuinely expires when the ad says it does. Flag and reconcile against the offer matrix effective window.

parameters.judge_focus: Approval-odds claims ('90% approval odds', 'outstanding approval odds'): does the integration type support them (lender-decisioned prequal vs partner odds model)? Is there a substantiation basis mapping the number/label to realized approval rates for this channel? Flag any odds language lacking a documented basis.
violation_examples: 90%+ approval odds for members like you (partner similarity model; realized approval rate for the channel is 61%)
Outstanding approval odds — you're practically in!
parameters.compliant_contrast: Based on ClearPath's review of your profile, you are prequalified. Final approval depends on a full application.
parameters.note: citation_quote is null because the cited FTC press-release page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching at authoring time; no quote is reproduced rather than quoting from memory.

rules.explanation: FTC v. Credit Karma: odds/likelihood claims must be substantiated by realized approval rates for comparable applicants; unsupported odds framing is deceptive.

parameters.judge_focus: Any approval-odds framing on mortgage prequal creative: Reg N 1014.3(q) bans misrepresenting approval likelihood outright — treat numeric odds claims on mortgage as presumptively non-compliant, not merely unsubstantiated.
violation_examples: 92% approval odds on your refinance — see your rate now
Outstanding odds of mortgage approval for homeowners in your area
parameters.compliant_contrast: See personalized rate estimates in minutes. Prequalification is not a loan approval.
parameters.citation_quote: The consumer's ability or likelihood to obtain any mortgage credit product or term, including but not limited to misrepresentations concerning whether the consumer has been preapproved or guaranteed for any such product or term

rules.explanation: On mortgage creative, approval-likelihood claims sit under Reg N's explicit prohibition rather than the general substantiation standard — severity is elevated to critical.

parameters.judge_focus: Testimonials/endorsements: is any material connection (payment, free product, affiliate bounty) disclosed unavoidably in the same medium as the claim? Do experience claims ('I save $400/month') represent generally achievable results, with generally-expected performance disclosed?
violation_examples: "ClearPath cut my monthly payments in half!" — Jessica M. (paid testimonial, no disclosure, atypical result)
Influencer video: "this loan changed my life, link in bio" with #ad buried twentieth in the hashtag block
parameters.compliant_contrast: "Consolidating with ClearPath simplified my bills." — Jessica M., compensated ClearPath customer. Savings vary; typical customers reduce their rate by 3-5 percentage points.
parameters.citation_quote: Endorsements must reflect the honest opinions, findings, beliefs, or experience of the endorser.

rules.explanation: FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR 255, 2023 revision): material connections must be clearly and unavoidably disclosed; there is no 'results not typical' safe harbor — atypical results require disclosure of generally expected performance.

parameters.judge_focus: Testimonials/endorsements: is any material connection (payment, free product, affiliate bounty) disclosed unavoidably in the same medium as the claim? Do experience claims (rewards earned, credit-score improvement) represent generally achievable results?
violation_examples: "I earned $2,000 in rewards my first year!" (top 1% spender presented as typical, no disclosure)
Creator reel praising the card with the affiliate bounty never mentioned
parameters.compliant_contrast: "The cash back adds up on groceries." — Marcus T., compensated reviewer. Typical cardmembers earn $180/year at average spend.
parameters.citation_quote: Advertisers are subject to liability for misleading or unsubstantiated statements made through endorsements or for failing to disclose unexpected material connections between themselves and their endorsers.

rules.explanation: FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR 255, 2023 revision): material connections must be clearly and unavoidably disclosed; atypical results require disclosure of generally expected performance.

parameters.judge_focus: Testimonials/endorsements on mortgage creative: material-connection disclosure, generally-achievable results, and Reg N overlay — testimonial content may not carry misrepresentations the lender could not make directly (rates, savings, approval).
violation_examples: "ClearPath got me approved when no one else would!" (approval-likelihood claim laundered through a testimonial)
"We saved $900 a month refinancing." (atypical savings, no expected-performance disclosure, no material-connection disclosure)
parameters.compliant_contrast: "The prequalification process was fast and clear." — Dana R., compensated ClearPath customer. Your savings, if any, depend on your current loan and qualified rate.
parameters.citation_quote: Advertisers are subject to liability for misleading or unsubstantiated statements made through endorsements or for failing to disclose unexpected material connections between themselves and their endorsers.

rules.explanation: FTC Endorsement Guides plus Reg N: endorser statements are the advertiser's claims; a testimonial cannot launder a prohibited mortgage misrepresentation.

parameters.check_description: A 'won't affect your credit score' claim is flagged until the flow is verified as soft-pull end-to-end before final application.
parameters.note: soft_pull_verified is a verification input, not an OfferCell column; the checker resolves it from integration config or emits a needs-verification finding.

rules.explanation: Soft-pull claims are conditional truth claims about the integration: deceptive if any step before final application triggers a hard inquiry. Flag for verification of the prequal flow configuration.
